summary: CLI exit codes for scan success and fatal parse error
description: The command-line entry point exits 0 when a scan writes valid JSON, and exits non-zero when a fixture is malformed enough to be a fatal parse error.
scope: Add main(argv) in src/living_graph/cli.py that scans a root and writes JSON
Success case: tests/fixtures -> exit code 0 and an output file exists
Failure case: a tiny malformed fixture raises a fatal parse error -> non-zero exit code
acceptanceCriteria: Running the CLI against tests/fixtures writes JSON and returns 0. Running it against a malformed fixture returns a non-zero code.
constraints: Strict TDD: write the failing test first and run it before implementation.
Do not add work beyond this task.
Do not add UI, watcher, or CLI code unless this task explicitly requires it.
Do not start a watch loop.

subtasks.title: Exit 0 on success, non-zero on fatal parse error

dataExamples: Malformed robot file with an unclosed section or invalid syntax returns not 0.
businessRules: main returns an int exit code; tests do not need to spawn a subprocess if they call main().
A fatal parse error is an exception from the Robot or Python parser, not an unresolved keyword.

Run python -m pytest tests/test_cli_exit_codes.py -q and confirm failure.
Run python -m pytest tests/test_cli_exit_codes.py -q and stop when it passes.
